title: Period, Domain, and Range of a Scaled Sine Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain, range, amplitude, and period of the function f(x) = 2*sin(3x) - 1.

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Period
steps.explanation: The sine function accepts any real number input, so 3x can be any real number, giving domain (-inf, inf). With frequency coefficient B = 3, the period is compressed to 2*pi/3.
steps.why: Sine is defined everywhere on R; multiplying input by B compresses the fundamental 2*pi period.

steps.title: Determine the Amplitude
steps.explanation: The leading coefficient A = 2 stretches the oscillation vertically so that it oscillates 2 units above and below its midline.
steps.why: Amplitude represents half the distance between minimum and maximum functional outputs.

steps.title: Calculate the Range via Extrema
steps.explanation: Because sine is bounded within [-1, 1], scaling by 2 gives [-2, 2], and subtracting 1 shifts the interval down to [-3, 1].
steps.why: Linear transformations preserve order and map closed intervals continuously to closed intervals.
